original_question: Does every finite 3-group T have a nontrivial characteristic subgroup C such that if T is a Sylow 3-subgroup of a finite group G, then T ∩ G′ = T ∩ H ′, where H = NG(C)? Such a characteristic subgroup is known to exist in p-groups for p ⩾ 5(G. Glauberman, Math. Z., 117(1970), 46–56), and for p = 3 there are two characteristic subgroups K1, K2 such that T ∩ G′ = (T ∩ H1′)(S ∩ H2′), where Hi = NG(Ki) (G. Glauberman, J. Algebra, 648(2024), 62–86). The group S4 shows that no such characteristic subgroups can be found in some Sylow 2-subgroups.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.50 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)".
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the official formulation. It has the right ambient objects (a finite 3-group T and a finite group G with T as a Sylow 3-subgroup), the right unknown object (a nontrivial characteristic subgroup C of T), the correct associated subgroup H = N_G(C), and the exact target equality T ∩ G' = T ∩ H'. It also preserves the motivating context given in the paper: the positive result for p >= 5, the two-subgroup result for p = 3, and the negative Sylow-2 comparison via S4.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, specify that C is a characteristic subgroup of T, i.e. C char T, with C != 1.
Make the quantifier over ambient groups explicit: the condition should hold for every finite group G having T as a Sylow 3-subgroup.
Define the notation G' and H' as the derived subgroups [G,G] and [H,H].
Write the normalizer explicitly as H = N_G(C).
If the motivational p = 3 comparison is retained, define H_i = N_G(K_i) and keep the Sylow-3-subgroup notation consistent throughout.
refined_question: For every finite 3-group T, does there exist a nontrivial characteristic subgroup C <= T such that, for every finite group G having T as a Sylow 3-subgroup, if H = N_G(C), then T ∩ [G,G] = T ∩ [H,H]?
justification: The notebook's official target is exactly this open problem: Problem 21.50 asks whether a single nontrivial characteristic subgroup of an arbitrary finite 3-group can control the intersection of the Sylow 3-subgroup with the derived subgroup of every ambient finite group in which it occurs as Sylow. The same entry immediately gives the intended nearby scope: the analogous single-subgroup statement is known for p >= 5, a weaker two-subgroup statement is known for p = 3, and Sylow 2-subgroups need not admit such a subgroup. No broader reformulation or paper-internal equivalent statement is supplied there, so the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is the official question with notation expanded.
